flagship.title: Long Valley Farm, beyond the field edge
flagship.standfirst: An easy two-mile loop from old farm fields into longleaf pines, with an optional millpond detour and plenty of room in the plan for Rupert’s pauses.
flagship.why_this_week: The attraction here is the change of scene within a modest walk: open field, the Rockefeller farmstead and a sandy return through the pines. Follow the white-circle Rockefeller Loop from the welcome-center fence opening; the official two miles describe the complete loop. This is a little more walking than last Thursday’s pine circuit, with farm history and an optional millpond peninsula rather than another forest-only plan. Keep the main loop as the default. Add Cypress Point only if Rupert and the footing are comfortable. Saturday is the better forecast starting point; Sunday currently carries a 50 percent chance of showers. Neither day is a weather clearance, and the forecast can change before the weekend.

access.name: Long Valley Farm parking, 2505 Long Valley Road, Spring Lake
access.parking: Use the designated Long Valley Farm visitor lot at the park office and welcome center, 2505 Long Valley Road. The Rockefeller Loop begins at the opening in the fence near the welcome center. Free day use. Saturday October 31: 8 a.m.–8 p.m.; Sunday November 1: 8 a.m.–6 p.m. Finish in daylight, before either closing time.

dog.water: Carry drinking water and a bowl; no dog swimming is part of this outing.
dog.shade: The route moves between open field, longleaf pines and woodland; shade is not continuous.

panels.label: One complete loop
panels.text: The official Rockefeller Loop is two miles, easy, and begins at the opening in the fence near the welcome center. Stay with the marked Long Valley Farm route.

panels.label: Share the trail
panels.text: Hikers and bicyclists use the loop. Keep Rupert on his attended six-foot leash, pause at the side when needed, and leave the farm structures undisturbed.

artwork.brief: Restrained environmental mode after six-plate visual review: the last four prints use flat burgundy frontal walking, ochre ball close-up, cream reclining and olive standing profile; W41 uses landscape motifs. Choose a seated three-quarter Rupert framed by autumn oak leaves, layered trunks and carved woodland depth. Keep Plate 006 face/build, mustard collar and a slimmer tapered American Labrador tail. This breaks the four-plate minimal-field run through pose, subject scale, spatial layers, cream openings, engraving density and woodland framing; not a field-colour swap. No documentary destination or activity claim.

local_trail.title: Turn back before the farmstead
local_trail.line: Use the beginning of the Rockefeller Loop as a short out-and-back and choose the turnaround by Rupert’s pace. Do not claim the full loop as completed.

pivot.if: Thunder, unsafe wind, flooding, slippery footing or an official closure
pivot.note: Postpone. A picnic or another outdoor trail is not a thunderstorm alternative; recheck official status and NWS before leaving.

conditions.trail_note: Stay on the marked Long Valley Farm loop and give bicycles room. Carry water even in late October; wet sand, roots and leaves may be slippery. The millpond is scenery, not a swimming stop.

practical.best_window: Prefer Saturday morning in daylight, with water for the warm afternoon. Recheck Sunday’s shower forecast. Sunday closes at 6 p.m. and the clocks return to standard time; do not use Saturday’s 8 p.m. hours for both days.
practical.fees: No day-use entrance fee; reservations and special permits are separate.
bring: Attended six-foot leash and waste bags
